**Purpose:** the single place to look for what was tested, what was found, and the raw proof behind it.
**Latest run (N):** `Runs/2026-08-05_114315/` · **`QA_MsSQL`** · **747 flows · 5,430 cases · 5,416 executed ·
1,388 endpoints · 5 h 29 m** — `OBJ-010`
**Previous run (N-1):** `Runs/2026-07-29_181439/` · **326 flows · 1,868 calls · 870 endpoints · 3 h 11 m**
**Generated by:** `tools/chain_runner.py` over `generate_flows.py` + `generate_data_flows.py`
(744 of 747 flows machine-generated)
**Retention:** every run is kept, nothing is deleted.

while failing validation** — a status-only assertion would have called every one of them green. **19

Read `Summary/OBJ-010-Execution-Benchmark.md` first — it is the N-1 vs N benchmark and the management
summary. The workbook is `Runs/2026-08-05_114315/QA_MsSQL_API_Execution.xlsx` (9 sheets, including

report: §below. How generation and chaining work: `../docs/briefs/overview.md`.

⚠️ **A resumed run's `meta` understates itself.** `chain_runner` records `elapsed_s`, `calls` and
`downtime_events` for the **current process only**. `2026-08-05_114315` ran in two segments, so its
`results.json` reports 94.9 min and 0 downtime pauses against true totals of **329.1 min and 17 pauses**.
The recovered figures are in `tools/.obj010/segments.json`, and the workbook reads them. Check
for this whenever a run folder was resumed.

⚠️ ISSUE-010's cause is unchanged: `GetLogs` / `GetErrorLogs` still hang 30 s and stop the IIS app pool.
They remain blocklisted. Do not remove that blocklist.

## 1. ✅ Everything here is retained

**Nothing in this folder is deleted or overwritten any more.** Each execution writes into its own dated
folder, so runs accumulate and can be compared against each other. The auto-delete that earlier harnesses
performed was removed on 2026-07-29.

| Folder | Contents | Lifecycle |
|---|---|---|
| `Runs/<YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS>/` | **One folder per execution** — `RUN_REPORT.md`, `results.json`, `evidence/*.json`, and the workbook where one is produced | ✋ **retained forever** |
| `Summary/` | Management-facing reports, authored | ✋ retained |
| `Issues/*.md` | Defect write-ups with evidence citations | ✋ retained |
| `SpecCache/` | Cached Swagger specs, shared across runs | 🔄 refreshed in place |
| `_archive-pre-2026-07-29/` | All output from before the retention change — the devint and outage runs, plus the Evidence folders that ISSUE-001…008 cite | ✋ retained |

Run-folder suffixes name the harness that produced them: no suffix = `chain_runner.py`, `_legacy-get` =
`run_qa_mssql.py`, `_swagger` = `run_validation.py`, `_derived-chains` = `run_chains.py`.

⚠️ **The scripts moved.** They live in `tools/`, not `Reports/Scripts/`. Their `baseline*.json`
files moved with them and sit beside the code, never under output.

## 2. How to run it

**API chaining — the current demo** (`chain_runner.py`, three declarative flows):

```powershell
python tools\chain_runner.py --dry-run                    # plan only, ZERO HTTP calls
python tools\chain_runner.py --execute                    # all three flows
python tools\chain_runner.py --execute --flow user_lifecycle
python tools\chain_runner.py --execute --probe            # also record response shapes
```

Flows are data, in `tools/flows/*.json` — add a file and it is picked up automatically. Full
explanation of the seven layers and the generation model: `../docs/briefs/overview.md`.

**QA_MsSQL — the legacy surface**:

```powershell
python tools\run_qa_mssql.py                  # 178 gated GET endpoints
python tools\run_qa_mssql.py --dry-run        # plan only, zero HTTP calls
python tools\run_qa_mssql.py --limit 25       # small smoke run
python tools\run_qa_mssql.py --promote-baseline
```

Reads `pam_BaseAPIURL` and the credentials straight from `Environments/QA_MsSQL.properties` — nothing is
hardcoded. The bearer token comes from `$PAM_API_TOKEN` or `tools/.token`; `chain_runner.py` generates one per run and caches it to `tools/.token_cache.json`. Dynamic
`getToken()` generation **now works** — the properties file held a stale password (ISSUE-009, resolved
2026-07-29). Generate a token **once** and reuse it; repeated `/arcontoken` calls locked this account.

**API chains — all five verbs** (`run_chains.py`):

```powershell
python tools\run_chains.py                                  # PLAN ONLY - zero HTTP calls
python tools\run_chains.py --allow-verbs GET,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE --depth 3
python tools\run_chains.py --execute                        # GET-only chains
python tools\run_chains.py --execute --allow-verbs GET,POST,PUT,PATCH
python tools\run_chains.py --execute --allow-verbs GET,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE `
       --allow-destructive --approver "<name>"
```

Chains come from `artifacts/graph/api-graph/out/api-graph.json` — rebuild that first if `APIConfig.java`
or the payload helpers change. **Nothing is issued without `--execute`.** Deny-by-default:
`GET` only unless widened, destructive actions need a named approver, 250 ms throttle, a
**circuit breaker** that aborts after 3 consecutive 5xx, a 200-call cap, and a pre-flight health probe
that refuses to start against a sick environment.

**devint — the Swagger microservices surface:**

```powershell
python tools\run_validation.py                # GET, zero-parameter tier
python tools\run_validation.py --tier extended
```

### ⛔ Safety gate (enforced at endpoint resolution, so blocked calls are never issued)

| Blocked | Count | Reason |
|---|---:|---|
| `GetLogs`, `GetErrorLogs` | 98 | Hang 30 s and stop the IIS app pool — **ISSUE-010** |
| `SetStatus` | 49 | Mutation declared as GET — **ISSUE-011** |
| Non-GET verbs | 997 | Default-deny, awaiting an approved allowlist |

Every exclusion appears in the workbook's *Excluded* sheet with its reason. Nothing is silently skipped.

No arguments are required. There is no endpoint list to maintain — the harness discovers the API from
the developer-shared Swagger sheet on every run, so an endpoint added by the developers appears in the
next report automatically.

## 4. The seven validation layers

Status code alone is not a test. Each endpoint is assessed on all seven, reported as its own column:

| Layer | Checks |
|---|---|
| **L1** `http-status` | Actual status against the codes the spec declares |
| **L2** `envelope` | Body `StatusCode`/`Message`/`errorCode` consistent with the HTTP status |
| **L3** `schema` | JSON Schema conformance against the spec's declared response schema |
| **L4** `required-fields` | Every schema-required property present and non-null |
| **L5** `types` | Each present property matches its declared type |
| **L6** `content-type` | JSON declared ⇒ JSON returned (catches HTML/plaintext error pages) |
| **L7** `latency` | Within the SLA budget (2,000 ms) |
| **DIFF** | Structural fingerprint compared against the approved baseline |

**L2 is the layer that matters most for PAM.** The product answers HTTP 200 with an application-level
`errorCode` in the body, so a harness checking only the status code would report a green build while
every endpoint rejected every request.
